summary: A 1932/1934 Forest Service L-4 lookout in North Cascades National Park, transferred to NPS in 1968 and still staffed each summer, reached only by a 10-mile trail.

facts.design: L-4 ground cabin, 14.25 x 14.25 ft, no catwalk

access.note: Active staffed NPS lookout reached only by a 10-mile trail; not a public rental.

facts.agency: National Park Service (originally U.S. Forest Service, Mount Baker National Forest)

events.note: NRHP/Wikipedia dates the current structure to 1934.
Staffed in winter 1943 by the Aircraft Warning Service to watch for enemy aircraft.
North Cascades National Park created; area and lookout transferred from Forest Service to NPS.
Added to the National Register of Historic Places February 10, 1989.

evidence.supports: built 1932 by USFS, L-4 ground cabin, 10-mile trail, staffed guard station, transferred to NPS in 1968, still staffed
evidence.quote: Copper Mountain Lookout, a L-4 ground cabin without catwalk, was built on Copper Mountain by the U.S. Forest Service in 1932... accessible only by a 10 mile trail, it was staffed each summer as a lookout and a wilderness guard station. With the creation of North Cascades National Park in 1968, the entire area was transferred to the National Park Service.

evidence.supports: built 1934, dimensions, roof, windows, AWS use in 1943, one of three remaining, NRHP listing date
evidence.quote: The Copper Mountain Fire Lookout was built in 1934... The lookout measures 14.25 feet (4.34 m) by 14.25 feet (4.34 m) square... During the winter of 1943 the lookout was staffed by the Aircraft Warning Service and used to watch for enemy aircraft. It is one of three lookouts remaining in North Cascades National Park from the Forest Service administration.

evidence.supports: built about 1932, staffed every summer, NHLR listed
evidence.quote: Built about 1932, this gable-roofed L-4 cab is staffed every summer and is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says 1932 (likely the original lookout post date); NRHP/Wikipedia say 1934 for the current structure. Both years are reported in the story.

notes_for_editor: Build-year conflict (1932 vs 1934) resolved by reporting both with their likely explanation, per brief's own flagged conflict.
